title: Clothes Labels in Larger Print
transcript:
A clothing shop in Linton has changed the way it displays care instructions. Customers buying coats and knitwear can now request a separate card with washing information printed in large letters. The usual small labels remain inside the garments, but staff say many customers find them difficult to read, especially when several languages share a tiny piece of cloth.

The idea came from a customer who accidentally washed a wool jacket in hot water. She could read the price label but not the instructions inside. When she returned to explain what had happened, the manager realised that staff were regularly answering similar questions over the telephone.

The first version of the cards used coloured symbols without words. During a trial, customers interpreted some symbols differently, so the shop added short written instructions. Each card now includes the product number, allowing customers to match it to the right garment even after the packaging has been thrown away.

The cards are free and are printed only when requested. The manager says printing one for every item would create paper waste without necessarily helping the people who need them. Staff will show customers a sample at the payment desk. A nearby shoe shop is considering a similar service, although it wants to include advice about cleaning different materials rather than copy the clothing cards exactly.

questions.prompt: What new service does the clothing shop offer?
options: Large print cards explaining how to wash clothes.
Telephone orders for all knitted garments.
questions.answer: Large print cards explaining how to wash clothes.
questions.explanation: 店铺提供单独的大字卡片，方便顾客阅读洗涤说明。

questions.prompt: What made the manager recognise the need for the service?
options: A printer offered the shop a discount.
A customer reported damaging a jacket after misreading its care information.
Staff asked to spend less time at the payment desk.
questions.answer: A customer reported damaging a jacket after misreading its care information.
questions.explanation: 一位顾客因看不清护理说明而用热水洗坏羊毛夹克，促使经理注意到问题。

questions.prompt: Why were words added to the original cards?
options: The product numbers were too long.
Customers preferred black and white printing.
The cards had to advertise a new collection.
Customers understood some symbols in different ways.
questions.answer: Customers understood some symbols in different ways.
questions.explanation: 试用时顾客对部分图标理解不一致，因此卡片补充了简短文字说明。

questions.prompt: Why are the cards printed only on request?
options: To keep the product information secret.
To reduce the number of products sold.
questions.explanation: 经理认为为每件商品都打印一张会浪费纸张，因此按需免费提供。
